title: Securities Dealing Policy and Guidelines (with Additional Dealing Restrictions for Restricted Persons)

tiers.name: Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All Directors, officers and employees of FPHC and its subsidiaries who intend to deal in FPHC securities. Subject only to the fundamental insider trading prohibition (no dealing, advising or tipping while holding material information); no blackout, clearance or instrument-specific restrictions.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors; the Chief Executive and all senior officers (all Chief Executive direct reports); trusts and companies controlled by such persons; anyone else notified by the Chief Financial Officer; and other key management personnel. Subject to black-out periods, prior written notification and consent, and post-dealing advice. 'Control' is judged by how decisions are made in practice, not technically.

windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the half-year results are released to NZSX

windows.start_anchor: 30 days prior to FPHC's year-end balance date
windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the full-year results are released to NZSX

windows.start_anchor: 30 days prior to release of a prospectus for a general public offer of the same class of Restricted Securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: None stated. The Chief Financial Officer may add persons to the Restricted Persons tier by notification, but no one is given power to impose additional black-out periods.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Securities' and 'Restricted Securities' extend to financial products issued or created over or in respect of FPHC securities, including warrants and other derivative products created by third parties, with no venue limit, and dealing includes agreeing to buy or sell securities. An OTC put/call with a bank is therefore a dealing in Restricted Securities requiring prior written notification to the CFO and consent of two Approvers, outside black-out periods, and no material information.
rules.evidence: the term "securities" also extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities issued by FPHC (for example, warrants and other derivative products), whether or not the financial products are created by FPHC or by third parties.

rules.detail: Non-Restricted staff face no clearance or window requirement; derivative products over FPHC securities are 'securities' and dealing in them is barred only while holding material information.
rules.evidence: If you possess "material information" ... you must not: deal in FPHC securities (including the exercise or cancellation of any options)

rules.detail: Hedging, limiting economic risk and protection of unvested or vested incentive securities are not mentioned anywhere. A hedge implemented through a derivative product is caught only as a dealing in Restricted Securities (see derivatives rule).

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar are not named. Any agreement to sell FPHC securities, or a financial product created in respect of them, is a dealing requiring prior consent outside black-out periods.
rules.evidence: "dealing" in securities is a broad concept and it includes buying or selling shares, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent, and the exercise or cancellation of options and the entering of agreements to buy or sell securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned and is not within the dealing definition.
CFDs are not named but are financial products created by third parties in respect of FPHC securities and therefore Restricted Securities; dealing requires consent and is barred in black-out periods.
rules.evidence: financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities issued by FPHC (for example, warrants and other derivative products), whether or not the financial products are created by FPHC or by third parties.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not prohibited or regulated; it is referred to only in the exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale, which implicitly contemplates Restricted Persons holding FPHC securities under margin lending arrangements. Entering the loan itself is not a 'dealing' (no encumbrance limb) and so needs no consent.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of FPHC that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage or lien over FPHC securities is not mentioned and is not within the dealing definition, which is confined to buying, selling, agreeing to buy or sell, and exercising or cancelling options.

No restriction on borrowing against FPHC securities. The exclusion for disposals resulting from 'a secured lender exercising their rights' assumes secured financing over FPHC securities is permissible; any enforcement sale is excluded from the additional restrictions but remains subject to insider trading law.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of FPHC that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. However, such dealings are still subject to the prohibitions against insider trading

rules.detail: No short-term, speculative or minimum holding period rule.

clearance.approver: Any two directors of the company, or a director and the Chief Financial Officer ('Approvers'), after written notification to the Chief Financial Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly following completion of any dealing
clearance.section: Requirements before dealing; Requirements after dealing
clearance.evidence: A consent is only valid for a period of 15 trading days after notification. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to dealing.
further more specific and stringent rules also apply to trading in FPHC's securities, by Directors and certain employees

exceptions.approver: Approvers (any two directors, or a director and the CFO)
exceptions.evidence: Consent to trade during a black-out period will only be granted if the application is accompanied by sufficient evidence (in the opinion of the Approvers) that the sale or disposal of FPHC's securities is the only reasonable course of action in the circumstances.
Exceptional circumstances for these purposes include severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the Approvers.
or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the Approvers.
participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the FPHC (eg applying for an allocation of securities under an employee equity plan offer).

acquisition of FPHC securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of FPHC securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of FPHC securities through a rights issue
the disposal of FPHC securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of FPHC securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary)

exceptions.approver: FPHC consent via Fixed Trading Plan Consent form
exceptions.evidence: trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan during a black-out period, the plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan once the plan has begun and the plan cannot be cancelled before the expiry of the fixed period of the plan
a disposal of securities of FPHC that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

external_documents: Securities Markets (Disclosure of Relevant Interests by Directors and Officers) Regulations (NZ)
exemption_authority: The Board may approve updates, amendments to and exemptions to the policy, implemented by posting on the intranet. Approvers (any two directors, or a director and the CFO) may consent to dealing in a black-out period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order, or anything they deem exceptional) where sale or disposal is the only reasonable course; such consent is valid 5 business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The additional dealing restrictions set out above do not apply to ... a disposal of securities of FPHC that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. However, such dealings are still subject to the prohibitions against insider trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank enforcing security over collared shares (even in a black-out) does not breach the policy, though the executive remains exposed to insider trading law if enforcement is discretionary while they hold material information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no prohibition on margin lending, secured financing, hedging, short selling or short-term trading; the only rules are insider trading, black-outs and consent for Restricted Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the shares, is not a 'dealing' and requires no consent; only the derivative legs are regulated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the term "securities" also extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities issued by FPHC (for example, warrants and other derivative products), whether or not the financial products are created by FPHC or by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call is a Restricted Security, so entering, unwinding or physically settling the collar requires Approver consent outside black-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Request for Consent form: '6. To be Transacted: On NZSX / Off Market Trade / Other Specify'; '3. Type of Transaction: Buy / Sell / Transfer'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The consent form expressly accommodates off-market and 'other' transactions, so an OTC collar can be described and cleared through the standard process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consent is only valid for a period of 15 trading days after notification. A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of material information prior to dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within 15 trading days of consent and becomes unexecutable if material information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where securities in FPHC granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with the Securities Dealing Policy and Guidelines and the additional dealing restrictions set out above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vested shares released from a plan are ordinary Restricted Securities; unvested plan securities are not separately addressed, so a collar over them is not policy-prohibited but plan terms should be checked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons will be considered responsible for the actions of trusts and companies controlled by them. In this respect, 'control' is not to be construed in a technical way but by looking at how decisions are made in practice.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or company controlled in practice by the executive is treated as the executive's own dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities Dealing Policy and Guidelines (2013 final), dated 27 August 2013.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy pre-dates current ASX Guidance Note 27 expectations on hedging and margin lending, so the company may have adopted a later version; confirm currency before relying on the absence of restrictions.

summary: A funded collar over vested shares is possible under this 2013 policy. The purchased put and written call are financial products created over FPHC securities and therefore 'Restricted Securities', so a Restricted Person (director, CEO direct report, KMP or their controlled trust or company) must notify the CFO in writing and obtain consent from two directors or a director and the CFO, execute within 15 trading days, deal outside the black-out periods (30 September to the half-year results release, 30 days before balance date to the full-year results release, and 30 days before a prospectus), hold no material information, and advise the CFO promptly afterwards. The loan secured on the collared shares faces no restriction: margin lending, secured financing, hedging and encumbrances are not regulated, and a secured lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the additional dealing restrictions (though still subject to insider trading law). Non-Restricted employees need no consent at all. Unwind, roll or physical settlement of the collar by the executive is a fresh dealing requiring new consent outside black-outs, and the 2013 date suggests confirming the policy remains current.
